newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- NOV 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Clean up at the Athens Stock Exchange. The issue of wide-ranging reforms to the bourse is on the agenda following last week's developments and the closure of the bourse for the first time in its history. ASE President Emmanuel Xanthakis was non-commital on whether he would resign last night and bickering brokers were still undecided whether they would allow trading at the bourse today. The government, however, will proceed with measures to pull the bourse into line, doubling the fines and sending finance ministry inspectors into firms to examine portfolios.

--A new opinion poll shows main opposition New Democracy supporters unhappy with their leadership options. Athens Mayor Dimitris Avramopoulos, who has not yet said he will contest the leadership, pulls 27.9 percent of the vote, while former prime minister and party leader Constantine Mitsotakis garners 18.3 percent. ND leader Miltiades Evert and his main contender George Souflias tie at 15.0 percent.

--Interior and Public Administration Minister Alekos Papadopoulos warns that the next two years will be tough. "Greece needs some good house-cleaning," Papadopoulos says. "Everyone has to be aware that we will not make it if we did not accept that 1997 and 1998 will be tough years, years of sacrifices".
--New Democracy deputy Constantine Karamanlis says he will not refuse a challenge, implying that he will contest the leadership of the main opposition party at the forthcoming congress.
--Another three judges face disciplinary procedures while more charges are expected within the week.
--New Democracy leader Miltiades Evert reacts against weekend comments by party cadres. The party's Political Council will meet tomorrow to consider disciplinary procedures.
--The government's plans for spending cutbacks draws fire from local government. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
